subject: ancientTreant
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: ancient treant, walking tree guardian.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a TypeScript module for a Warcraft-style treant creature—a chunky, mossy humanoid tree about 4 meters tall with glowing eyes and root-like feet—using the SDK's builder tools for joints, chains, sweeps, and textures. I'm sketching the skeleton structure starting from the hips.

Now I'm working through the full joint hierarchy: a spine chain from hips to chest to neck to head, thick trunk-like legs with hip joints reaching the ground, and arms with twig-finger digit chains, plus a head built from separate upper and lower jaw pieces. I'm pinning down exact coordinates for each joint—hips, chest, neck, head—to keep the proportions right at roughly 4.2m total height, and working out how the spine chain's catmull curve and named joints should connect properly to the parent hip joint.

Adding torso loft stations...

I'm defining the moss-over-bark paint logic using noise thresholds, then setting up leg limb chains from hips to feet with bent knees and tapered sweep radii per side, plus root-claw toe spikes fanning forward from each ankle.

Now for the arms, I'm laying out a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain per side with slightly extended rest-pose coordinates, planning to connect them as a catmull or polyline path with named joints.

For the hands, I'm building each as a sphere-ish palm at the wrist with four finger chains plus a thumb, each finger made of two joints parented to the wrist tip, swept thin and tapering like twigs with spiked tips pointing down and slightly forward.

Now I'm moving to the shoulder area—adding mossy burl spheres and shelf fungi as pauldron detail, and sketching branch chains that sprout from the head crown upward and outward using catmull curves with leaf cards attached.

I'm figuring out the leaf placement along branches using sweep frames with the head bone as the joint, then pushing those frames into an array to feed into the card-generation call with size, lean, and variation parameters.

For the treant's canopy, I'm thinking of clustering several flat-shaded icosahedron blobs in dark green attached to the head bone, then scattering leaf cards across their surfaces to build a fuller crown like an Ancient Protector's foliage.

For the head itself I'm planning a trunk-face design: a scaled sphere cranium, boxy brow ridge, knotty cone nose, and a separate lower jaw part hanging off a jaw joint with mossy roots for a beard. For the eyes I want glowing amber sockets using a decal technique—placing a textured eye image onto the skull surface with a dark socket and bright glowing center.

Calculating eye placement on the sphere surface so the decal projects correctly at roughly z=0.73-0.8, then working out the mouth and jaw geometry - a nose cone pointing forward, an upper jaw box for the muzzle, and a lower jaw joint aimed forward from around y=3.3.

I'm adding the lower jaw box with hanging beard sweeps from the chin dotted with moss, plus a couple root-fang tusks and small upward spikes. I'm positioning a tilted brow box above the eyes and planning bark-branch antler horns instead of ears, then thinking through the texture set - eye decals, glowing runes, moss tufts, maybe mushrooms - with a glowing heartwood rune cavity for the chest.

Now I'm defining the torso as a vertical loft, placing a glowing rune decal on the chest and a hollow knot at the belly, then setting loft stations up the spine at increasing heights with varying width and depth to shape the bark body.

For the waist, I'm adding a scaled sphere for the hips and building a root-like skirt as a ring of spikes hanging down from the pelvis, computing each spike's direction by blending its outward axis with a downward pull so the roots splay outward and droop naturally.

Now I'm adding moss patches at the shoulders using tinted spheres, and shelf fungi scattered across the torso as small flat orange cylinders stuck onto the surface at several scattered hit points.

Placing feet beneath the ankles with boxes at ground level, then spawning toe spikes fanning forward from each foot with tapered radii. I'm adjusting leg thickness along a tapering radius function so thighs read bigger than ankles.

Setting up the inverse-kinematics leg chains with hip pivots, bend directions, and distance checks so lengths comfortably reach their foot targets on each side.

Now I'm placing bark spikes along the arm sweep using dorsal normals from frame samples, then arranging leaf cards similarly across those same arm frames. For the head crown, I'm sketching antler point paths rising from the skull toward a tall peak, keeping the overall height suitably oversized for a giant treant.

Working through the center branch paths and their sub-spike placements, with leaf cards distributed along each catmull path oriented by tangent direction. I'm also positioning rounded icosahedron blobs clustered near the top-back of the head to form the crown mass, varying their radii and offsets for an organic silhouette.

I'm checking overlap between the crown blobs and the skull/face geometry, nudging the hair mass back in z so it sits above the brow without covering the face, then adding a mossy cape of scattered cards across the upper back using a normal-based filter to target back-facing surfaces.

I'm planning the texture set: leaf, eye, rune, and tuft SVGs, possibly adding a second gold-toned leaf variant so card picks have more variety. For the leaf I'm sketching a gradient-filled leaf shape with a vein line, and for the eye texture I'm drawing a dark almond shape with an amber inner iris and a pale slit pupil to give it an angry look.

Now I'm working out the orientation — figuring out which side of the model is which from the viewer's perspective so the eye's slant (tilted down toward the nose for an angry expression) mirrors correctly between left and right.

Then I'm setting up the decal call for placing the eye, positioning it relative to center with the correct size and mirror flag depending on side. I'm also noting the import path concern for the glow kit, since the task specifies every SDK export should come from a single module, so I need to double check whether pulling glow from the kits subpath is still valid.

For the heart decal I'll draw a dark filled oval with glowing rune strokes layered on top, keeping it transparent elsewhere so it cuts cleanly against the torso. I'm now working through the skeleton's arm chain naming (shoulder/elbow/wrist per side) and sweep radii for limbs, making sure hands and arms connect properly with added burl and elbow branch details, then moving into the rig's joint names starting with hips and spine.

I'm continuing to define the spine chain (spine1, spine2, chest) and head/jaw joints with the hips as the root, then sketching out a short neck connecting to the chest—adding it as an extra loft station on the torso so the head sits naturally on top.

Now I'm placing the jaw and head joints with their orientations, then building the mouth parts: a lower jaw box with chin, an upper muzzle box, and a skull sphere positioned so there's a visible gap between upper and lower jaw for the mouth opening.

Adding teeth and tusks...

Beard strands and length adjustments...

Now working on angry eyebrows, tilting them to slope downward toward the center for a fierce expression.

For the nose, I'll shape a cone-like knot nose angled forward and slightly down, and for the head's material I'm leaning on bark tones with mossy highlights, considering saturated amber/gold cracks for a chunky, stylized woodland look.

I'm adding vine wraps around the torso using a surface loop near chest height, nudging the loop placement to avoid clipping the arms, then layering extra vine rows and mushroom studs around it for added texture.

Setting up helper functions now for vectors, along-path leaf placement, and typed frame arrays so the code compiles cleanly. Writing berry clusters...

For crown and shoulder foliage I'm scattering leaf cards across surface parts derived from the blob geometry, aiming for around 60 hits each. I'm adding a shoulder pad as a scaled sphere bonded to the shoulder joint, painted with a mottled moss texture, then wrapping up the final export metadata.

Now I'm fine-tuning the feet: checking the foot box sits right at ground level with a slight sink, positioning toe spikes angled downward with tips near the base, and confirming the ankle joint and leg tube radius line up correctly at the foot. I'm wiring the toe parts to the leg's tip joint for rigging, and considering adding a few splayed root spikes jutting outward and backward from the base of each foot for a grounded, rooted look.

Now I'm defining the bark and moss paint functions for the torso and limbs — setting up a grain texture for the base bark color, layering moss patches using noise where surfaces face upward, and creating a darker bark variant for shading. I'm also setting up loft options for the limbs, tying stations to the spine bone with color assignments.
